A font here is a font DATA ASSET (UDreamUIFontData_BaseObject), not an FSlateFontInfo: the size is Style.FontSize and the outline is in the text style, and the three together are what UMG packs into one struct. GetFont/SetFont read and write Style.Font, so the typeface obeys StyleSource like the rest of the look.
Writes Style.Font and re-pushes. Null means "leave the paragraph on the font it has", which is every field that exists today -- a style only ever adds a typeface, it cannot take one away.

ONE material for the whole paragraph rather than one for the font face, because that is what the text renderer takes. The control forwards it (SetFontMaterial/GetFontMaterial) onto the VALUE's paragraph only -- a material meant for a password field's glyphs has no business on the words "Enter your name".

The outline and the glyph face are drawn by ONE pass of one SDF material here -- the outline is a distance threshold inside it, not a second draw with its own material. There is no separate channel for a material to be assigned to.

Raising the keyboard here IS beginning the edit: ActivateInput summons it (subject to VirtualKeyboardTrigger) and DeactivateInput puts it away. There is no keyboard to toggle independently of the edit that needs it.

Slate's integrated keyboard is an in-viewport keyboard WIDGET the platform layer swaps in for consoles. This library draws its own UI in world space and has no such widget, nor a platform road that would supply one.
No asynchronous typeface-face load to paint around: the library renders from its own font data assets.
Same reason as FontFacesLoadingPaintPolicy.
